disclaimer: Pre-diagnose maximizes the probability that the downstream reproducibility check passes on the first try by removing known avoidable failures. It does NOT guarantee a first-try pass.

risks.message: Author should keep filenames and `do/source` include paths consistent; renames must update all references.
risks.predicts: A do/source/import target does not resolve to any file shipped in the package.

risks.message: Author should not `cd` into a subdirectory mid-script before relative file paths; it breaks when the package runs from the root.
risks.predicts: Relative `cd` mid-script breaks relative paths when run from the package root.

risks.message: Author should set a seed before any stochastic operation (sampling, simulation, bootstrap, multiple imputation), so the draws are reproducible; without one, every run produces different numbers than the paper.
risks.predicts: Stochastic operation with no seed; a re-run draws different numbers than the paper reports.

risks.message: Author should mark which block of code builds which reported table/figure with a `* --> Table N` (or `* --> Figure N`) comment, so the model->table-cell mapping is explicit.
risks.predicts: Multiple estimations with no `-> Table N` comments anchoring the table<->command mapping.

risks.message: Author should save each reported table's estimates and each figure to a designated relative output subfolder — a path ending in tables/ for tables or figures/ for figures (e.g. output/tables/, results/tables/, or a bare tables/) — so every paper artifact has a regenerating command and a known output location.
risks.predicts: Estimation/figure present but no export saves the artifact to a relative output/ folder.

cannot_predict: Numerical match of coefficients (random seeds, solver behavior, hidden transforms surface only at execution).
Full environment reconstruction (external repos / OS libraries / licensed software may still fail).
Diagnostic fidelity (instrument strength, model classification need real outputs).
Runtime completeness (long scripts, memory, encoding, platform differences are execution-time facts).
Repository acceptance (external validation and human review may add rules).
